object_description: low compact square building with courtyard
design_condition: The low square building follows the existing geometric order, but its sunken sports and break areas create cramped transitions and only partially integrate with the terrain.

positive.statement: The concise volumetrics provide a simple and convincing starting position.
The courtyard and diagonally offset staircases create exciting, usable cluster units.
The technical facade elements give the building an appropriate public appearance.
The compact arrangement leaves usable land reserves for later development.
The upper-floor plan demonstrates convincing potential in lighting and orientation.

negative.statement: The allocation and terrain integration of the outdoor spaces remain only partially understandable.
The transition to the sunken fields contradicts the intended continuous outdoor space, while the forecourt appears cramped.
The sports court lacks the spaciousness needed for the intended central outdoor space.
The access system is inefficient and requires additional escape stairs because of the distances.
The narrow spaces and small atriums on the classroom floors are critical.
The complex support system entails high costs.
The organization of the floor plans is complicated and sometimes labyrinthine in operation.
